summary: The Complete COVID Collections Act focuses on overseeing, investigating, and collecting funds related to COVID-19 small business relief programs. It requires the Small Business Administration to refer certain unpaid COVID-19 loans under $100,000 to the Department of the Treasury for collection decisions, extends oversight authorities, establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for fraud enforcement on specific relief programs, mandates regular reporting from federal agencies regarding fraud and collections, and requires recovered fraud funds to be applied toward reducing the federal debt.

affected_groups.effect: Their loan collection claims must be referred by the Small Business Administration to the Department of the Treasury for final collection decisions.
affected_groups.group: Small businesses and borrowers with COVID-19 related loans under $100,000

affected_groups.effect: Subject to a standardized 10-year statute of limitations for criminal charges or civil enforcement actions regarding certain loans, grants, and investments.
affected_groups.group: Entities investigated for COVID-19 relief fraud

affected_groups.effect: Subject to expanded oversight, mandatory coordination, and regular reporting or briefing requirements concerning relief funds, collections, and fraud prosecutions.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Small Business Administration, Department of the Treasury, Department of Justice, Pandemic Response Ac

key_provisions: Extends the authority and expiration date of the Special Inspector General for Pandemic Recovery to September 30, 2030, and expands its oversight to Small Business Administration programs.
Sets a 10-year deadline for filing criminal charges or civil enforcement actions against businesses, states, or municipalities for fraud related to specific COVID-19 relief and loan programs.

Requires the Small Business Administration to refer claims for collection on COVID-19-related covered loans under $100,000 to the Department of the Treasury, which will make final decisions on suspension or collection.

Requires the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to provide monthly briefings and personal annual testimony to congressional committees regarding loan collections and improper payments.
Requires the Attorney General to submit monthly reports to Congress detailing Department of Justice prosecutions, recoveries, referrals, and declined cases related to COVID-19 programs.
Requires the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee to maintain a public website displaying real-time data on federal recoveries of covered funds.
Mandates that any funds recovered from fraud in a covered program must be applied solely to reducing the federal debt.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact total dollar amounts or exact numbers of loans currently in suspension that will be affected by the referral requirement.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Complete COVID Collections Act focuses on overseeing, investigating, and collecting funds related to COVID-19 small business relief programs. It requires the Small Business Administration to refer certain unpaid COVID-19 loans under $100,000 to the Department of the Treasury for collection decisions, extends oversight authorities, establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for fraud enforcement on specific relief programs, mandates regular reporting from federal agencies regarding fraud and collections, and requires recovered fraud funds to be applied toward reducing the federal debt.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation alters the oversight and enforcement framework for pandemic relief funds by extending investigation windows, tying debt collection processes directly to the Treasury, and mandating transparent reporting of fraud recoveries.
